absent: Locking, synchronization and memory ordering rules for virtual CPU, hypervisor per CPU and guest state are not shown.
Secure monitor call dispatch, argument passing and return conventions beyond identifier construction and lifecycle grouping are not shown.
Complete guest exit handling, world switch and timer, VGIC and tracing operation semantics are not shown.
32-bit condition evaluation internals and full nested fault forwarding beyond predicate results are not shown.
Page table, address translation and TLB maintenance behavior beyond fault address helpers and guarded translation outcome are not shown.

findings.text: Two address fault helpers are specified. One derives a hypervisor fault address value from a physical address report by selecting a middle bit range and shifting it down by a byte offset. The other isolates the low page offset from a fault address.

Exception reporting uses a small constructor pairing a numeric class code with its display name, and a table built from it enumerates trap reasons known to the hypervisor including unknown, wait, coprocessor and system traps, floating and vector extensions, calls, aborts, alignment, debug and return categories.
Processor mode reporting maps each exception level stack pointer variant from EL0 through EL3 and each legacy 32-bit privileged mode to a short human readable label for diagnostics.

Virtual CPU reset defines three canonical status words. The 64-bit EL1 and EL2 variants select the privileged high stack mode with asynchronous abort, interrupt, fast interrupt and debug events masked. The 32-bit variant selects supervisor mode with its asynchronous, interrupt and fast interrupt masks set.

Guest exit status packs two pieces of information. A flag in bit 31 records whether a system error is pending alongside the exit, and the remaining value carries a small exit reason. Interrupt is 0, EL1 system error is 1, trap is 2 and instruction length fault is 3, while hypervisor gone aliases a stub error value. A companion table maps reasons to short names.

Host to hypervisor calls are encoded as vendor specific fast 64-bit secure monitor calls indexed by a small integer function number, with the initialization function numbered zero. The hypervisor vector reserves space for two instructions before the handler entry.

Hypervisor call availability follows a protected mode lifecycle. An early group covers setup before finalisation, a finalise call transitions state, a middle group stays always available for core run control and maintenance, and a late group becomes available only after finalisation for memory ownership and virtual machine lifecycle. Boundary markers delimit the groups and a maximum marker ends the enumeration.

Non virtualized host initialization passes a parameter block grouping memory attribute and translation controls, thread pointer, hypervisor stack virtual and physical addresses, page table physical address, hypervisor configuration, and stage two translation controls.
Hypervisor stack unwinding state records a normal stack base and an overflow stack base together with the current frame pointer and program counter.

Symbol visibility distinguishes virtualized host and non virtualized host builds. Declaration helpers introduce either a plain external symbol, a prefixed non virtualized variant, or both, and per CPU variants follow the same split for host versus hypervisor storage.

Symbol selection adapts to build and runtime mode. Single mode builds resolve directly to the active variant and to an undefined sentinel for the inactive one, per CPU accessors follow the same rule, and combined builds dispatch at runtime on whether the kernel runs in hypervisor mode.

Non virtualized per CPU access derives an address from a per CPU hypervisor base table plus the offset of the requested object from the per CPU area start for the current or a named CPU, yielding null when the base for that CPU is not established.

Kernel symbol references resolve to the linear alias when executing outside hypervisor mode and to the original address when already in hypervisor mode, with a convenience form applying the rule to non virtualized hypervisor symbols.
Three hypervisor entry aliases select the mode appropriate implementation for initialization, the exception vector, and the branch predictor hardening vectors.

Address translation instructions execute under a fault guard. The wrapper saves processor state, attempts the translation with a follow up synchronization barrier, and on fault restores saved state and reports a memory fault through an exception table entry linking the attempt to its handler.

Hypervisor context register layout places general registers at eight byte stride from the user register base, with the link register at the thirtieth slot position and the EL0 stack pointer immediately after it.

Hypervisor tracing reuses remote event machinery with a fixed architecture header and event section, thin wrappers for structure and print arguments and field definition, a single event constructor, and a flag enabling multiple reader support.

Exception vector selection uses four spaced offsets for current level with different stack pointers and for lower level 64-bit and 32-bit guests. Offsets start at zero with successive 512 byte steps. Synchronous, interrupt, fast interrupt and system error types start at zero with successive 128 steps, each paired with a short name.

Guest fault injection provides narrow wrappers. Data and instruction aborts forward to a common synchronous exception injector distinguished by access kind and fault address, plain system error injection marks the syndrome as implementation defined, and nested vector trapping synthesizes a syndrome with the vector class and length bit before nested synchronous delivery.

Whether guest EL1 is 32-bit is determined either from the hypervisor configuration width control or from a virtual CPU feature flag depending on build. Hypervisor configuration reset initializes guest flags only before first run and additionally enables a memory management trap when the hardware lacks stage two forced write back. Run once status follows from whether a host thread is attached.

Virtual CPU state access exposes pointers to hypervisor configuration, program counter, status word and virtual error syndrome within the saved context, with helpers to test 32-bit mode, validate conditions only for 32-bit guests, set Thumb mode, and read or write general registers with zero register semantics where reads yield zero and writes are ignored.

EL2 and hypervisor context tests interpret saved status and configuration. EL2 detection checks privileged mode, effective virtualization controls account for capability absence and a documented implementation choice forcing an abort mask in one configuration, hypervisor context combines EL2 mode with virtualization controls, and host versus nested classification plus nested error state follow from those results.

Nested virtualization is gated by build mode, hardware capabilities and per VM or per CPU features. Separate checks cover overall nesting enablement, two levels of fractional feature support, and a stricter nested configuration requiring host extension plus specific virtualization controls. System register reads apply sanitized masks for nested guests, and host extension presence uses fast paths for hypervisor only code.
Two headers use conventional include guards to ensure single inclusion of hypervisor assembly and emulation definitions.
External field preparation helper relied upon for syndrome construction, owned by another dossier.
External build configuration test relied upon for nesting checks, owned by another dossier.
